His absence will open up a space for another wide forward, with Noni Madueke pushing for a call-up with his form for Arsenal.

Industry observers note that good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

According to recent reports, whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant problem of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

The squad will be released at 10am and followed by Tuchel’s explanations, which we will also cover here, an hour later.

Latest Update: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh row over a record-breaking EU loan to European aerospace firm Airbus could reopen a long-standing rift with Washington and threaten an existing EU-US trade truce.
  • The European Investment Bank (EIB), the lending arm of the EU, agreed in June to loan Airbus up to €3 billion ($3.4 billion) but US President Donald Trump's top trade advisor recently suggested the loan breached a 2021 EU-US agreement on state support.
  • It has been revealed that "I had sincerely hoped that trade-distorting European subsidies to Airbus were a thing of the past," US Trade Representative Jamieson Grier said in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh row over a record-breaking EU loan to European aerospace firm Airbus could reopen a long-standing rift with Washington and threaten an existing EU-US trade truce.

The European Investment Bank (EIB), the lending arm of the EU, agreed in June to loan Airbus up to €3 billion ($3.4 billion) but US President Donald Trump's top trade advisor recently suggested the loan breached a 2021 EU-US agreement on state support.

It has been revealed that "I had sincerely hoped that trade-distorting European subsidies to Airbus were a thing of the past," US Trade Representative Jamieson Grier said in late October. "For decades, France, Germany and Spain have aggressively supported Airbus, their national champion aircraft manufacturer, to gain an unfair advantage over US aerospace workers and business.".

He also suggested there was a lack of transparency around the terms of the loan. The EU insists the loan does not amount to subsidies, that it is in close contact with the Office of the US Trade Representative and "will provide all necessary information," a spokesperson told DW.

An Airbus spokesperson told DW the company is "actively engaging with the relevant authorities and are happy to share more information about the loan with governments.".

Airbus and the US company Boeing, the world's two largest plane manufacturers, were previously involved in a 17-year corporate trade dispute.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) ruled that both the EU and US provided the companies with state subsidies, resulting in years of tariffs, tit-for-tat retaliation and claims of victory by both sides.

A deal to end tariffs with strict provisions on state support was finally agreed in 2021 and strengthened in 2025, but the latest row threatens to reopen the dispute and could potentially threaten the wider EU-US tariff deal agreed last year, experts say.

The previous Airbus-Boeing dispute was one of the longest-running corporate disputes in history and led to billions of dollars' worth of tariffs leveled by both sides.

"Trade experts tend to hate to talk about it because there are so many ups and downs to the story, it took so long to get resolved and it always tends to creep back up again," Inu Manak, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics who specializes in international trade law and policy, told DW.

Sources indicate that she notes because the issue is such a "persistent thorn in the side," it has the potential to spiral, but for now the US is only signaling displeasure before things escalate. "They want to talk about this, and that conversation will need to happen before anything goes further," she mentioned.

At the heart of the current dispute is whether the €3 billion loan from the EIB, the largest corporate loan ever authorized by the bank, amounts to illegal state support.

"The EIB loan to Airbus is a standard loan on market terms," a European Commission spokesperson told DW. "It carries interest, it must be repaid in full, and it is the type of financing the EIB provides every year to companies across many sectors.".

A spokesperson for the bank told DW the €3 billion loan is "a standard EIB corporate loan, implemented under the bank's established procedures and on market-based terms." It says it considers the financing to be "fully consistent with the market-terms principle" of the 2021 deal.

A spokesperson for Airbus told DW the loan is "a standard corporate financing facility, similar to commercially available loans we've signed in the past.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Fredrik Erixon, founding director of the European Center for International Political Economy, indicates the lines are still blurred when it comes to what counts as a subsidy and what is just a loan and that only a comprehensive World Trade Organization investigation could establish the full facts.

Another potential issue is how the €3 billion will be used, including the share earmarked for research and development and how much funding will support defense-related activities versus commercial aircraft development.

Inu Manak indicates it is impossible at this point to determine if the loan amounts to the provision of illegal subsidies or not, and that it depends on the very specific terms of the credit provided and whether or not it could be proved to be damaging to Boeing's business.

Recent findings suggest that "If it's a market-based loan, if it's not providing below-market rates that would provide an unfair advantage, then it should be fine," she said. "That remains to be seen.".

In Erixon's view, the situation is further complicated by the fact that the aerospace sector is "a highly murky business" due to the amount of defense contracts companies like Boeing and Airbus hold with governments and the high costs associated with that in terms of research and development.

"The problem is we've ended up in a world where there's only two large aircraft manufacturers," he told DW. "And it is a business with high upfront costs when you're going to develop different things.".

He points out that while Boeing may have a legitimate grievance over this loan, Airbus and the EU can point to Boeing's own deals with the US government.

Recent findings suggest that "Boeing does R&D contracts for military purposes, which end up producing technology and support for the civil aircraft program for Boeing," said Erixon. "That's also what the World Trade Organization found previously.".

Recent findings suggest that it was Boeing that originally asked the US trade representative back in July to intervene over the loan, linking it to Airbus' initiative to develop a new single-aisle aircraft program, which could spark a new era of intense competition between the two giants. Neither the US trade representative nor Boeing responded to a DW request for comment.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Inu Manak thinks the next obvious step for the US would be to launch a Section 301 investigation, which is an official inquiry to determine if the loan "violates an international trade agreement or is unjustified, unreasonable or discriminatory, and that burdens or restricts US commerce.".

She thinks the Trump administration has no interest in engaging with the WTO and believes it has the potential to threaten the broader EU-US trade agreement.

In a recent development, "I don't think there's a lot that can stop the US trade representative from taking action if they decide they want to do it," Manak remarked. "They may think there may be something else to extract from the European Union.".

Fredrik Erixon agrees that "it's going to be a point of leverage that the Americans can use against Europe," adding that the dynamics underpinning the aerospace sector — that both Boeing and Airbus need greater government investment due to ramped-up military spending — is the fundamental underlying problem.

Recent findings suggest that "We are getting into a state aid race, which basically means these companies just need more and more and more money," he said. "That in itself is an escalatory development.".

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

In a recent development, portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's new full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

Sources indicate that they are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The upcoming national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

His form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

But it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

The attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he stated: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the substantial-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the looks, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

In a recent development, but things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

Recent findings suggest that by the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

According to recent reports, if Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he unveiled himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

Recent findings suggest that 'Today is a dream come true,' he said after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of new manager Jorge Jesus.

When pressed if he was the upcoming permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he stated.

Then he added: 'We know it's a massive, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

It remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

Solanke blocks Calvert-Lewin’s goalbound header from the corner and Elvedi heads the rebound wide from two yards!

Leeds have a throw on the right that Ampadu tosses into the box. Van de Ven heads it out. Amapdu tackles Tonali and sends Bogle down the right and Van de Ven shins it out for a corner, thrusting out a leg to stop Calvert-Lewin having a tap-in.

Leeds make a change at left-back:.

Sources indicate that and he’s straight into the action as Nmecha sends him on the overlap down that wing. His cross is good but Van de Ven heads it out to Ampadu whose shot from 18 yards is blocked.

According to recent reports, he says the game isn’t played in slow motion and in real time you could tell it was accidental and there was no violence. He feels if the ref was advised to go to the monitor he would have had to send him off had he looked at the slo-mo but that the VAR was protecting him from that outcome by not telling him to go to the screen as it did not warrant Bogle being sent off when watched at full speed.

Re the ‘penalty’, TNT Sports also indicates a replay from behind that suggests it was the point of Fernandes’ shoulder that was struck by the ball, not the biceps below the sleeve as it seemed from front-on.

That was a tough first half on the eye. Neither team are taking many risks and at the moment look like they would be happy with a draw. Perhaps these 12.30pm kick-offs need time to warm-up. James Maddison on the bench is an option to liven things up.

Two contentious incidents: Leeds could have had a penalty and could also have been reduced to 10 men. As for the actual match as an attacking spectacle? Nothing much to report. Spurs have threatened on the break, Leeds started well with a host of crosses but have fizzled out as Spurs’ midfield got a grip.

Spurs have a throw-in by the right corner flag but Porro’s pass goes straight to a Leeds’ defender.

Nmecha keeps the ball in play as it rolls down the left touchline but his cross is blocked out for a throw-in by Van Hecke. He also wins the header from Amapadu’s long throw.

Leeds have a throw-in high on the right. Ampadu will hurl it in. Spurs win the header.

Muharemovic wipes out Amapadu and Spurs have the numbers to punish Leeds but Porro’s cross hits the first defender and goes out for a throw-in, from which Porro fizzes over an uncontested cross.

Kudus whips a low cross/shot through the six-yard box that needed only a touch but Gray didn’t see it until too late and didn’t react in time.

Looks like six minutes of stoppage time.

Marmoush trips Muharemovic. Tel indicates he can’t continue before Leeds take the free-kick.

Bogle crosses from the right, Calvert-Lewin flicks it on and Nmecha heads it at the keeper. De Zerbi is playing merry hell with the fourth official over Bogle not being carded at all for that foul on Tel.

“What the f--- is going on?” chant the Leeds fans. Frustratingly long delay for VARs Tony Harrington and Matthew Wilkes to determine whether Jayden Bogle should be sent off for a tackle. He trod on Mathys Tel’s left foot, then clattered into his opponents’ right knee. It was ugly but not a red card, and should not have taken several minutes for the decision.

Porro tries to pass with the outside of his right foot into the box that goes straight through to the keeper.

Industry observers note that ‘What the f--- is going on?’ chant the crowd. VAR belatedly says it is not a red card offence.

VAR check continues for two minutes.

Tel is hurt by Bogle after the right-back accidentally, I think, trod on his left Achilles. Oddly no yellow card. VAR check for a red card.

Misunderstanding between Elvedi and Trafford makes a gift of a corner to Tottenham when the centre-back’s headed backpass goes beyond the keeper who had come too close. Marmoush heads over at the back post.

Nmecha butchers a good position for Leeds with a stray pass to Tanaka but Leeds win it back, feed Nmecha who 20 yards out, has the space to shoot but tries to find an offside Calvert-Lewin instead.

Ampadu tackles Gray, shifts the ball to Tanaka who sends Gudmundsson down the left but his long cross is picked off by Kinsky.

Recent findings suggest that omar Marmoush is not quite there as a No9, or False Nine. His runs are not on the shoulder of the last defender and timing is off with team-mates.

Sources indicate that kudus’s daisycutter of a shot from 25 yards is saved by Trafford to his right. Lots of sighs, chelping and audible signs of concern from the home fans.

According to recent reports, tel floods into space down the left and passes infield to Marmoush who opens his body with a touch to set up a right-foot shot from the D that hits Muharemovic’s foot and Trafford saves low to his right. Kudus was in a great position on the right but Marmoush took it on himself.

Tottenham have definitely settled into it now and the nerves of the home crowd are palpable as Trafford punches Porro’s cross away and then Tel shoves Bogle in the back to give Leeds a free-kick.

Recent findings suggest that gray leads the Tottenham press as Leeds struggle to play out. Bogle’s flick yields possession and Longstaff is booked for a foul when trying to win it back off Fernandes.

Longstaff and Ampadu defend nervily but efficiently to take the ball off Marmoush who was found by Tel’s pass in from the left.

Spurs have started to get the measure of the tempo now and are enjoying a spell of possession and probing.

Van Hecke wins the header from Longstaff’s free-kick and Spurs launch a counter-attack, first up the left then, after horseshoeing it over to the right where Porro’s pass looking for Kudus goes out for a goal-kick.

Van de Ven is booked for grabbing Bogle after being spun by the wing-back in the inside-right position.

Porro arrows a long cross down Trafford’s throat.

Leeds could do with a goal to reflect their good start. It’s been the story of their season that they haven’t been able to turn good performances into wins. Marmoush and Tonali have both been penalised, the former for hand ball, the Italian for a high boot when challenging Tanaka.

Gudmundsson roasts Porro down the left, cuts back his cross and Longstaff deflects it to Ampadu who hammers a swerving half-volley wide.

That Mateus Fernandes handball shout was in the category of: seen them given. He was leaning towards the ball and it looked like it struck some part of the upper arm, although the majority of contact was shoulder.

Sources indicate that leeds have a corner on the left after raining the box with crosses. Kinsky catches Longstaff’s cross. The home side are stopping Spurs playing out with a very high press.

The more often we see Fernandes’ incident, the more it looks like a stonebonker of a penalty. It rolled down his biceps.

Tanaka smacks a shot wide from the left of the D.

According to recent reports, tonali is the most advanced of Newcastle’s midfield. Longstaff, for Leeds, is on the right.

Leeds’ shout of hand ball when Fernandes chests Nmecha’s cross back to the keeper.

In a recent development, VAR is checking. He says it was the shoulder. Didn’t look like it to me.

Trafford catches Kudus’ loopy cross and sets Leeds off on an attack up the right and Van Hecke hacks Bogle’s cross away.

Tottenham kick off, attacking from right to left, towards the Gelderd End. They moves the ball back to Kinsky who moves it to Porro. The ball is played up the right looking for Kudus but Trafford comes off his line to lash it into the stands fr a throw-in.

It has been revealed that we keep pushing. Tough game for us. Tough game for them because we are in a good moment. We start every game 0-0, we have to work hard if we want to win the game.

In a recent development, pedro Porro can bring everything, fantastic guy, fantastic player. Nothing changes because he knows his position. We have a clear style. Nothing changes for us.

Archie Gray will make his first appearance against his old club today after joining Spurs from Leeds in 2024. He was an unused sub in the two matches last season but is now an established part of this De Zerbi resurgence, starting all but two matches in the current campaign. Gray was named in the England Under-21 squad yesterday but is heading in the right direction for a senior call-up.

According to recent reports, dominic Calvert-Lewin is starting for Leeds today, after doubts over a foot issue heading into the Elland Road fixture. He was named in the England squad yesterday, which suggested he was not ruled out of this clash against Spurs.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi has kept a settled team as he looks to make it four Premier League wins in a row. Dominic Solanke is dropped to the bench in his only change, with Pedro Porro coming in – so it may be Omar Marmoush playing as a central forward.

According to recent reports, there are many processes in [Tottenham’s] build-up. You need players to interpret this and the legs to cover the centre of the game. It is always complicated [tactically against a De Zerbi team], very dominant in possession. You have to find solutions to be competitive in this area.

Recent findings suggest that the most crucial thing is what happens on the pitch but [we have bought] Sean [in because of the] tactical aspect. He is sop smart, has experience and also the legs to compete. It’s necessary to have a third midfielder on the pitch to control their processes. On the other hand he is sharp on the offensive actions, many times. Lukas [Nmecha] brings the greediness, physicality and can take the attention off Dominic. he has been very sharp in training, scoring many goals and for that he has the chance to shine today.

Dominic is a key player and thank God he was able to join us in team training yesterday. Overall he is in a good position.

You will always have spells in the Premier League when you cannot convert good performances into results or when you can’t score many goals. We are struggling with injuries for key players in our attack – Noah Okafor, Anton Stach – but hopefully we have also turned the corner.

The pre-season, it was clear [he is] a special talent. You recognise the special talent immediately and he doesn’t need to show something special, you understand? Everything that he does and he is one of the special talents.

The next step he has to enjoy, he has to follow the older players, the players with more experience like [Andrew] Robertson, [James] Maddison, Ben Davies and to find the time to play.

It is my responsibility because when you manage young players and sucho significant talents like Luca, it is a bigger responsibility for me.

He has to be ready when he goes on the pitch. I think it [does] not depend on the result, he can play from the beginning. Before the Chelsea game, I thought to play with him in the first XI, but in the end you have to find the right moment and for them also.

Sources indicate that I think the age is not so important. The most important is the quality, personality, the behaviour on the pitch and the qualities. And Luca has all of these qualities.

Recent findings suggest that leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin suffered a medical emergency ahead of our Premier League fixture with Manchester United on Sunday 18 October at Elland Road. After being transferred to hospital, he was placed into a medically induced coma and sadly following a period of unresponsiveness, the decision was made to withdraw life support. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years. The thoughts of everyone at Leeds United are with Colin's family and friends at this sad time. We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November.

May be 4-3-3 with Archie Gray there against his old club, moving up from right-back  rather than the World Cup winner Porro playing ahead of him on the right wing.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

In a recent development, daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

According to recent reports, they never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

Spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

Tel also scored in Spurs’ home game, a 1-1 draw in May, and then kicked Ethan Ampadu in the head to concede the penalty from which Leeds equalised. I wonder what kind of impact he will have today. Incidentally Roberto De Zerbi on his last visit to Leeds when manager of Brighton in 2022-23 had such a strop on the touchline when the home team equalised that he was within a gnat’s whisker of being sent off.

The Original Article was published on 01 July 2026.

Correction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10695-1 Published online 1 July 2026.

In the version of this article initially published, the reagent information for the DNA2 inhibitor was incorrectly reported as DNA2i; Sigma-Aldrich, SML4192 and should instead have read DNA2i; NSC-105808. The change affects the Methods “Thymidine analogue incorporation” section and the Supplementary Table 7 reagents sheet. The error has been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

To launch the release, current players recreated some of Eltonâs most famous album covers in full kit. Defender Kevin Keben channelled "Jump Up!" with a bowler hat, while Mattie Pollock paid tribute to "Rock of the Westies".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's the international break, and it's usually a quiet week in the world of soccer.
  • 14🇺🇸 NWSL semifinal: Washington Spirit vs.
  • According to recent reports, sunday, Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's the international break, and it's usually a quiet week in the world of soccer. Well, it wasn't the case. USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino will leave the American national team after the two Nations League's matches against Haiti and will become the upcoming manager of Manchester United, after the Red Devils declared the sacking of Michael Carrick. Pochettino, who was hired by the USMNT in 2024, will make his comeback in the Premier League after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. I'm Francesco Porzio with the latest.

Saturday, Nov. 14🇺🇸 NWSL semifinal: Washington Spirit vs. Utah Royals, 12 p.m. ➡️ CBS, Paramount+🇺🇸 CONCACAF Nations League: Haiti vs. United States, 4:30 p.m. ➡️ TNT, HBO Max🇺🇸 USL League One Final: Charlotte Independence vs. Athletic Club Boise, 7:30 p.m. ➡️ CBS Sports Golazo Network.

According to recent reports, sunday, Nov. 15🇮🇹 Serie C (Ronaldinho's comeback): Ravenna vs. Forlì, 11:30 a.m. ➡️ Paramount+, CBS Sports Golazo Network🇺🇸 NWSL semifinal: Gotham FC vs. Kansas City Current, 3 p.m. ➡️ ABC 🇺🇸 USL: Charlotte Independence vs. Athletic Club Boise, 7:30 p.m. ➡️ Paramount+, CBS Sports Golazo Network.

Industry observers note that now the massive question is about who will be the successor of Pochettino at the national team. With a fresh national training center, an established team, and young players coming up from everywhere to push that squad, it's a job that should be an attractive one to managers around the world, depending on the direction that U.S. Soccer wants to go. Pochettino was an appropriate splashy hire ahead of the World Cup, and it's not surprising that a top team in the world still wanted him. But when looking to build a stable base for 2030, there's a chance that the powers that be would prefer a candidate who would be more bought into American soccer. Here's some of the names that our own Chuck Booth wrote down:.

Steve Cherundolo, U.S. U-23s: Currently overseeing the U-23s, the former Los Angeles FC manager would likely be in the USMNT succession strategy for Pochettino. The goal was to bring both camps together as much as possible and ensure that they had a similar style, as plenty of players would go between both squads depending on needs. The issue is that this has all happened faster than anyone would've anticipated, since if Steve Cherundolo was going to take over the USMNT, that'd likely be a 2028 post-Olympic deal rather than right at this moment. But also looking at the performance of LAFC without Cherundolo, it's clear that he held things together plenty in that squad and that he could be a fit for the role; the question is just when.

Pep Guardiola, free agent: You have to make the call, and it looks like they will. We all know what the answer likely is, but if there's an opening and the USMNT wants the best manager available, Pep Guardiola is right there. The former Manchester City, Bayern Munich and Barcelona boss is expected to be their top target, according to The Athletic. They reportedly called Jurgen Klopp before hiring Pochettino, and this would be a similar scenario as Klopp is now with Germany. Guardiola isn't going to stay out of management forever, so why not try to bring him back in on the road to 2030? He would be facing similar concerns to Pochettino of not knowing if he'll be a long-term fit for the role, but those aren't things that should come into play if the goal is to hire the best available manager who is a fit for the job.

Roberto Martinez, free agent: A name that came up after the World Cup when decisions were being made on whether Pochettino should be extended, Roberto Martinez could come into consideration yet again. On paper, he offers a mix of European experience and the staying power of someone who has overseen multiple international sides for an entire cycle, but it's tough to say he'd be a good fit. Martinez wasn't able to lead Belgium's golden generation to a title and struggled to get Portugal to play to their talent as well. With a USMNT that have the world at their feet as young players begin to lead the way, it'd be better to go the domestic route before turning to Martinez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that two weeks after the U.S. men's national team failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup, an in-depth look at the man who would become the team's head coach seven years later was available on bookshelves across the U.K. and, eventually, everywhere else. "Brave Upcoming World" by Guillem Balague is just as much a glimpse at the 2016-17 Tottenham Hotspur team as it is at a manager on the rise in Mauricio Pochettino, who cut to the chase in a handwritten note before the first chapter.

"Football is," he wrote, "or at least to me, a context of emotions.".

There is supposed to be something ruthless about a sports team at the peak of its powers, and Pochettino's are no exception. He has built high-intensity, attack-minded teams for the better part of two decades, now on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean, but he has never tried to strip humanity out of a profession that unnecessarily demands an emotionless approach to the job. It is why, at U.S. Soccer's national training center in Atlanta on Friday, he began to cry.

"The human being is in front of everything," he said, "and that is why that is a really difficult decision, but we need to move forward. But a significant thank you from my heart.".

Pochettino finally booked his exit from the USMNT and will join Manchester United next week after two final games in the U.S., a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday. Though United's approach only began on Sunday, after Pochettino and his staff arrived in Atlanta for the latest international break, the move was in some ways years in the making -- he had longed for a return to the Premier League, and as the USMNT's first coach with genuine international appeal, he had already turned down several offers before the Red Devils came calling. He was never destined for a long stay with the USMNT, even if the four-year deal he signed in August indicated otherwise, and U.S. Soccer knew as much by including a $10 million buyout clause in the latest contract.

Recent findings suggest that call it What You Want: A weekly podcast where Jimmy Conrad, Charlie Davies and Tony Meola cover all things USMNT and the state of the beautiful game in the United States. Catch the show YouTube live every Tuesday and Friday at 10 a.m. ET.

The predictability, though, did not lessen the pain.

Pochettino did not answer questions about his legacy or discuss the appeal of the United job, but two years after U.S. Soccer's surprise coup, he finally offered a hint at why the USMNT gig appealed to him outside of the paycheck and excitement of a World Cup on home soil. He became the USMNT's head coach a few short months after exiting Chelsea despite the turnaround he was overseeing one year into the role -- he and the club's owners did not see eye to eye on what was next, and as a result, he initiated his own exit. He was one of several high-profile coaches in Europe's club game to drop out of that realm of the sport. Jurgen Klopp left Liverpool on a high and told CBS Sports a year later that he did not miss a thing about coaching, but he recovered from the mental exhaustion just in time to take the Germany job in late summer. Carlo Ancelotti is now in charge of Brazil, Thomas Tuchel is presently the England coach and Pep Guardiola also left Manchester City after a storied decade. Burnout was something at least a few of them name-checked on the way out, and in his own way, Pochettino concurred on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the most important thing is all that we left here [are] the moments that we share together," he said. "All the things that we accomplished. The things that we put in place. All the standards, all together, we increased in that federation and around the world, too, maybe. I didn't prepare [this] speech. I am talking with my heart and I want to say a big thank you ... because we recovered our motivation. We recovered our capacity to dream big, the capacity to train players that really want to improve and really want to share good moments and players that really care about the federation and this country.".

Sources indicate that if Klopp's timeline is anything to go by, two years appears to be the exact amount of time a coach needs to recover from the demands of soccer's most high-pressure environments before badly craving a return. Pochettino's U.S. arrival was a boon for the players, who had lost their way after a group-stage exit at the Copa America but now make up a team that has as clear a path forward as any. Forward Folarin Balogun remarked as much on Thursday, when Pochettino's exit was all but confirmed.

"I think things have been working well," he stated. "We have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different.".

Sources indicate that as it turns out, though, this job was just as meaningful for a coach who seemed to feel a little lost himself. In "Brave Newly introduced World," Pochettino established that there is no distinction between the person and the coach. "Football has made me who I am and who we are as a family," he wrote. "It's what we wanted and what we chose to be. The ball has to be our travelling companion.".

It is no wonder, then, that he needed a reset somewhere. Some will quibble that the USMNT job should not be the place for a mental reset, but the way Pochettino describes it, it was the right job at the right time for all involved. He did not describe the post as a break from his real calling but rather as one that reminded him why he got into this career in the first place. It is perhaps why United, a perilous job in which most are destined to fail, has its charms for a person like Pochettino. He feels ready for what might be an impossible job, and the window to take it before he becomes a has-been to Europe's top clubs is fleeting. There is also an undeniable truth about the profession Pochettino has chosen -- job security is a fictional concept and so failure is the only guarantee. Someone else's shortcomings are the only way to get a job in the first place, something Pochettino admitted as he celebrated a year with the USMNT in October 2025.

According to recent reports, "I think we knew something [was] wrong here because if not, the federation, why [would] they call us?" he said at the time. "Why [would] they offer the job, no, really with not too much time to build our ideas, set our principles [for] the World Cup?".

It has been revealed that U.S. Soccer has a fairly long runway this time to land a replacement, with the next World Cup just under four years away. The players, though, might feel left in the lurch for the time being as they watch a coach they really enjoyed working with say an abrupt goodbye. As Balogun put it on Thursday, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are.".

It has been revealed that pochettino's tenure was hardly perfect. The shockingly bad results outweighed the impressive ones, but most of the games landed somewhere in the unremarkable middle. There was plenty of hand-wringing along the way, from an almost incessant period of trial and error to his insistence that players be fully committed to the project when he would say things that led people to question his dedication. He also never got the team to a long-awaited World Cup quarterfinal, failing to reset the energy after the Balogun affair sucked the confidence out of the group. Yet he left quite the impression on some of the players he worked with. Take Sebastian Berhalter as an example -- he was as far away from the national team's radar as it gets when Pochettino first worked with him last year but has only hit stride after stride since. He credits Pochettino's belief in him for the rise, which is perhaps why he was nearly as emotional as the coach himself when he spoke on Thursday.

"Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter said. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach, and I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job, so he's meant a good deal to me for sure.".

It only makes the question of where U.S. Soccer goes from here so pressing. This was not a perfect tenure, and yet it hit the sweet spot of what all parties needed at this moment in time. That clearly includes Pochettino, who enjoyed the best of what the U.S. had to offer along the way, a celebrity of sorts in his own right. Maybe long stretches in the Southern California sunshine during the World Cup had an oversized influence, and "Take Me Home, Country Roads" slaps too hard when 60,000-plus sing it together. Whatever it was, the vibes, at their very best, were special. It is hard for a self-proclaimed "emotional guy" to deny that, even if he feels life needs to take him elsewhere.

"When this type of moment [arrives], [these] always are tough, tough moments because [these] are not easy decisions. Normally, it's the opposite. You know you will be sacked and you cry because you want to stay," he remarked. "A substantial thank you from my heart ... because you always were transparent and always you always put in front the interests of the federation but always trying to build something together and we really enjoyed. We learned a lot from you, from you all, from this country, [these] amazing people. Yes, I think it was one of the most difficult decisions in our careers.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While the winds of Manchester United swirl around the United States men's national team, there's still soccer to be played as a place in the Concacaf Nations League semifinals is on the line. Mauricio Pochettino will be managing his final games in charge of the national team, finishing out his tenure with the two matches against Haiti before returning to the Premier League. Given that Steve Cherundolo is currently with the U-23 side in Spain, there's no viable interim head coach that the USMNT could have gotten in before Tuesday anyway, meaning that Pochettino gets an unconventional farewell tour before leaving for Old Trafford.

In a recent development, the message from players such as Chris Richards and Antonee Robinson is that they're professionals, and considering that Richards could be going back to a latest manager at Crystal Palace following the break, these are elements of the game that they're used to dealing with. That professionalism is key when the singular focus has to be on getting past Haiti and into the Nations League semifinals.

According to recent reports, I already expected Pochettino to lean on the World Cup core of the roster in the first match, but given the vibes around the USMNT, it's even more important that they get off to a good start, as any doubt that's left opens the door for the noise from outside camp to set in. They've already dealt with this, considering the AC Milan rumors that cropped up ahead of the World Cup, and that will only make the squad more prepared to go out and perform even with the challenges at hand now.

Recent findings suggest that there are some fitness challenges to deal with, though. Folarin Balogun has been trying to earn a starting spot back at Monaco, and Pochettino has noted he's not 100% match fit. Weston McKennie has dealt with fitness issues, and Auston Trusty has also missed time due to the death of his father. If Pochettino determines that they can't start the match, there could be shifts in the XI, but the only player I see starting who wasn't a World Cup regular is Sebastian Berhalter.

With Gio Reyna withdrawn from the squad due to injury, Berhalter can deliver set pieces while also producing from the center of the pitch. He was one of the best performers from the September and October international breaks and has gone back to Middlesbrough and kept up his form, which should be rewarded during this camp. Sergino Dest has also left camp due to an injury, which leaves the wings a little lighter than expected, but Malik Tillman's versatility will come in handy as the Bayer Leverkusen man can fill any midfield position.

Breaking: 'F*** the Pope and the IRA' chant lands England in hot water as fans are given suspended one-game stadium ban and FA fined

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.
  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That said, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA stated: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

In a recent development, england supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

Industry observers note that the issue is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel mentioned.

'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.
  • Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.
  • "Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

Sources indicate that "Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp mentioned, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

Sources indicate that the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

In a recent development, it paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

According to recent reports, the 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

Recent findings suggest that "I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp remarked after the Netherlands match.

In a recent development, "We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

But Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," noted Klopp.

Sources indicate that scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

Sources indicate that "A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still noted it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Sources indicate that proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he said, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

While that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he mentioned. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

In a recent development, "We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he mentioned.

In Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

Mauricio Pochettino leaves incomplete legacy as USMNT tenure nears finish

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1231 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's the first thing that you hear from multiple people as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to oversee his final two games.
  • If his departure overshadows the performance on the pitch, leaving the USMNT without a chance to win the Concacaf Nations League final for a second consecutive tournament, that will undo a significant portion of the good that he has accomplished by bringing along younger members of the squad.
  • It has been revealed that date: Saturday, Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He raised the standard of U.S. Soccer. It's the first thing that you hear from multiple people as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to oversee his final two games. The reality is more mixed. His 1.91 points per game are the third-best of any manager to oversee the United States men's national team for more than 10 games, behind Gregg Berhalter and Bruce Arena, but he's also the first permanent manager since Steve Sampson to not win a Concacaf title, with the USMNT falling short in both the Concacaf Nations League and the Concacaf Gold Cup. That noted, it's hard to say that he isn't leaving the USMNT in a better place than he found it, although some credit should be given to U.S. Soccer and former sporting director Matt Crocker for that. It's a conflicted legacy that Pochettino will leave, but it's also one that can't be fully realized until after he oversees his final two matches against Haiti.

If his departure overshadows the performance on the pitch, leaving the USMNT without a chance to win the Concacaf Nations League final for a second consecutive tournament, that will undo a significant portion of the good that he has accomplished by bringing along younger members of the squad. But as he prepares to depart, the USMNT exited the World Cup in the round of 16, the same stage as in 2022, and questions remain about how they'll hold up against the world's top teams. With the 2028 Olympics coming up and a new training facility that allows space for the youth and senior sides to train in the same place, alongside the improvement in U.S. youth development thanks to MLS Next and MLS Next Pro, the USMNT were going to be in a good place no matter who took over at this stage, which is also what makes it critical to look at what comes next.

It has been revealed that date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Location: Nu Stadium -- Miami, Florida TV: TNT | Live stream: HBO Max Odds: Haiti +750; Draw +440; USMNT -350.

"Our ambition is high, and we believe that this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world. We have an experienced group of players; we've got a dynamic young pool of players," U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson said. "Last night, Mauricio, staff, and most of the men's team watched our U-20s play here at the national training center, which was a pretty special moment. We publicly shared our ambition is to be in a position where we're winning major tournaments, including World Cups, and we want to make sure that we're attracting leaders who help us do just that. We know from our experience that great leaders want to work with great people, and great leaders want to make an impact on things that matter, and we think that we've proven at U.S. Soccer that we're a great place to work and we're a great place to make legacy-defining impact.".

Call it What You Want: A weekly podcast where Jimmy Conrad, Charlie Davies and Tony Meola cover all things USMNT and the state of the beautiful game in the United States. Catch the show YouTube live every Tuesday and Friday at 10 a.m. ET.

Sources indicate that U.S. Soccer is still in talks to hire a director of soccer who will work with the incoming head coach, United States women's national team coach Emma Hayes and the rest of the U.S. Soccer staff to shape the vision of American soccer. The sport is growing rapidly here, which is what makes this such an attractive job even without the shine of hosting a men's World Cup on home soil to add to the sales pitch. Listening to Batson, while BJ Callaghan may be one of the top American fits for the role, you can easily see why the USMNT would like to bring in Pep Guardiola if they can, and there's a sales pitch there to at least get top targets to pick up the phone.

This doesn't diminish what Pochettino has done while leading the national team, but each manager has made his mark on American soccer in his own way. Jurgen Klinsmann added legitimacy to the USMNT role and ushered in an era of German Americans who led the squad to newly introduced heights. Gregg Berhalter came in, raised the floor for the squad, did excellent work with dual-national recruitment and led the squad out of its group at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Sure, in hindsight, things should've ended there, with U.S. Soccer moving in a different direction after the World Cup, but the players also wanted continuity.

It has been revealed that you can make the same argument that Pochettino maybe shouldn't have been signed to a new contract following the World Cup, but even he seemed to believe that an opportunity such as Manchester United wouldn't have come this quickly. If he were leaving in 2028, after Steve Cherundolo led the U.S. U-23s on a strong run in the Olympics, the departure wouldn't be as bittersweet as this one, which feels like a job left unfinished by the Argentine.

Sources indicate that pochettino did add confidence, and to hear players like Sebastian Berhalter, Cavan Sullivan, Alex Freeman and Neil Pierre, among others, tell it, when Pochettino was at his best, this team would press anyone off the pitch. Now the onus is on the players to take that forward under newly introduced management.

Sources indicate that "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win," Folarin Balogun said.

Sources indicate that "He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach.".

A tearful Pochettino and the disappointed players show that this didn't end the way anyone would've wanted, but that doesn't mean there isn't plenty of good to build on for whoever comes next. With Cherundolo leading the December camp, there's plenty of time to ensure that the next hire is the right one, but now that U.S. Soccer has shown that it can recruit a coach of Pochettino's caliber, there's no reason to stop there. Having a coach coveted by others is a product of success, but having a system that can move past that proves things are sustainable.

The word "sustainable" hasn't been one that U.S. Soccer has been able to use as of late, as one thing going wrong could lead to a spiral, but with benefactors, facilities and youth all at once, it's time to build a future that isn't dependent on who the coach is, because that's what will lead to winning a World Cup.

Breaking: Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row
